revision.body:
What does a derivative tell you?

\(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\) gives the tangent gradient for each admissible input. Imagine the secant moving until its two points meet.

How do roots and reciprocals differentiate?

Use \(\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dx}x^n=nx^{n-1}\) for a rational power on the domain where the required derivative exists.

How does the sign describe the curve?

A positive gradient means the curve is moving upwards as x increases at the point. A negative gradient means it is falling.

Quick worked example

A curve is defined by \(y=2 x^{3} - 5 x^{2} - 10 x + 8\).

Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).

Write square roots and reciprocals as rational powers before using the power rule.

\(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=6 x^{2} - 10 x - 10\)
revision.checks:
• Substituting a point into the original function gives its height, not its gradient.
  • A negative exponent becomes more negative when you subtract one.

addmaths-0606-d1-chain-rule.description: Identify the inner function before differentiating a composite power, root or reciprocal.

sections.title: Which function is inside the other?
sections.label: Inner outer

blocks.html:
Write \(u=g(x)\) for the inside expression and \(y=F(u)\) for the outside rule. Multiply the two rates.

\[\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm du}\cdot\frac{\mathrm du}{\mathrm dx}.\]

Substitute the original expression for \(u\) after multiplying.

figure.alt: Input x becomes the inner value u, and the inner value becomes the output y.
figure.caption: For \(u=2x+1\) and \(y=3u^2\), a change in \(x\) travels through both links. Multiply the derivative factors.

examples.title: Differentiate a square of a linear expression
examples.question:
The function is \(f(x)=4 \left(7 x + 1\right)^{2}\).

Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).
solution: Put \(u=7x+1\), \(y=4u^2\). Then \(\frac{\mathrm du}{\mathrm dx}=7\) and \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm du}=8u\).

examples.title: Find the gradient at a particular input
examples.question:
The function is \(f(x)=11 \left(7 x + 1\right)^{3}\).

Find the gradient at the specified input. Use \(x=4\).
solution: Put \(u=7x+1\) and \(y=11u^3\). Then \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm du}=33u^2\) and \(\frac{\mathrm du}{\mathrm dx}=7\).
The gradient function is \(33u^2\cdot7=231(7x+1)^2\). At \(x=4\) the gradient is \(231(29)^2=194271\).

examples.title: Keep the square-root factor in the denominator
examples.question:
The function is \(f(x)=10 \sqrt{x^{2} + 6}\).

Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).

  1. \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\frac{10 x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 6}} - 7\)
  2. \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\frac{10 x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 6}} + 9\)
  3. \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\frac{10 x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 6}}\)
  4. \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 6}}\)
solution: Let \(u=x^2+6>0\). For \(y=10u^{1/2}\), the outer derivative is \(5u^{-1/2}\). The inner derivative is \(2x\).
Multiply the two rates. The derivative is \(\frac{10x}{\sqrt{x^2+6}}\), option C.

examples.title: Explain why the gradient is zero at the origin
examples.question:
The function is \(f(x)=11 \sqrt{x^{2} + 5}\).

Find the gradient at the specified input. Use \(x=0\).
solution: Use \(u=x^2+5\) and \(y=11\sqrt u\). Multiplying \(\frac{11}{2\sqrt u}\) by \(2x\) gives \(y^\prime=\frac{11x}{\sqrt{x^2+5}}\).
At \(x=0\), the numerator is zero and the denominator is positive. The gradient is therefore zero.

examples.title: Rewrite a reciprocal square as a negative power

The function is \(f(x)=\frac{9}{\left(8 x + 8\right)^{2}}\). Work where \(8 x + 8>0\).

Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).

  4. \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=- \frac{18}{\left(8 x + 8\right)^{3}}\)
solution: Write \(y=9u^{-2}\), where \(u=8x+8>0\). Its derivative is the product \((-18u^{-3})(8)\).

Find the two derivative factors

If \(u=g(x)\) and \(y=F(u)\), then \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm du}\frac{\mathrm du}{\mathrm dx}\).

Worked example

For \(y=4(7x+1)^2\), \(u=7x+1\), \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm du}=8u\) and \(\frac{\mathrm du}{\mathrm dx}=7\). Thus \(y^\prime=56(7x+1)\).

Roots and reciprocals

Use a half-power for a square root and a negative power for a reciprocal. Keep the original domain.

addmaths-0606-d1-product-rule.description: Differentiate the product of two functions and use the result to find a tangent.

sections.title: Which factor stays unchanged?
sections.label: Keep a factor

blocks.html:
If both factors depend on \(x\), each contributes a change.

\[\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dx}(uv)=u^\prime v+uv^\prime.\]

Differentiate one factor in each term and keep the other factor unchanged.

figure.alt: A rectangle gains a top strip, a side strip and a small corner when both side lengths increase.
figure.caption: For \(A=(x+2)(x+1)\) with \(x>0\), one strip comes from the changing width and one from the changing height.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: For \(y=uv\), write \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=u^\prime v+uv^\prime\). Label both factors and their derivatives.

blocks.title: Differentiate two changing factors
blocks.prompt:
A curve has equation \(y=\left(x + 2\right)^{2} \left(4 x + 3\right)\).

Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).
blocks.hint: List both factors and both derivatives. In each product term, keep one original factor.
blocks.solution:
With \(u=\left(x + 2\right)^{2}\) and \(v=4 x + 3\), use \((uv)^\prime=u^\prime v+uv^\prime\).

\(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=4 \left(x + 2\right)^{2} + \left(2 x + 4\right) \left(4 x + 3\right)\)

Use both contributions

A curve has equation \(y=\frac{\left(3 x + 5\right)^{2}}{x + 9}\).

Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).
extraPractice.hint: Apply the chain rule to the whole squared numerator before differentiating the quotient.
extraPractice.solution:
Use \((u/v)^\prime=\frac{vu^\prime-uv^\prime}{v^2}\) with \(u=\left(3 x + 5\right)^{2}\) and \(v=x + 9\).

\(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\frac{\left(x + 9\right) \left(18 x + 30\right) - \left(3 x + 5\right)^{2}}{\left(x + 9\right)^{2}}\)

Answer: \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\frac{\left(x + 9\right) \left(18 x + 30\right) - \left(3 x + 5\right)^{2}}{\left(x + 9\right)^{2}}\).

revision.body:
Identify numerator and denominator

For \(y=\frac uv\), \(y^\prime=\frac{vu^\prime-uv^\prime}{v^2}\). Keep values excluded by the original denominator.

Worked example

For \(y=\frac{2x+1}{x+2}\), \(u^\prime=2,\ v^\prime=1\). The numerator of the derivative is \(2(x+2)-(2x+1)=3\). Thus \(y^\prime=\frac3{(x+2)^2}\).

• Reversing the order changes the sign.
  • Simplifying algebra does not enlarge the domain of the original function.

solution: Use \(h=9r\) to get \(V=\pi r^2h=9\pi r^3\) and \(\frac{\mathrm dV}{\mathrm dr}=27\pi r^2\).

examples.title: Convert a radius rate to an area rate
